D29·dvy6 — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.6 measures tiered verify on a REPLAY of the 1.1 fixture's nine tasks: the reference solutions as scripted sessions through the real driver and real gate commands, each spec test shipped with its task (as this repo ships tests), the plan in three phases, run-level gates (`node --test` full, `node scripts/related.mjs {files}` quick), three injected faults (1.5/1.6 overwrite formatPrice; 1.2 adds a module the README test reads from disk, which no import reaches), and a clean scenario; arms interleaved, 3 reps (test-e2e/drive-lanes/tiered-replay.test.ts → results/2.6-replay.json)
over: Agent reps of the 1.1 fixture per D7 (`node run.mjs`), or the fixture as written (spec tests in the skeleton, a plan verify per task)
because: The arms differ only in what the driver runs after a session, so agents add noise and cost and nothing else: 2.5's reps swung 410–1290 s on host load, while the fixture's whole gate costs ~0.1 s. As written, the fixture's full suite is red until all nine tasks are done, so per-task full verify cannot run on it at all; shipping each spec with its task makes `node --test` green after every correct task, which is the property a full gate has here. The replay is deterministic, so 'no failure missed' is checked exactly: every fault's task reopened, the final tree green.
